Package neqsim.thermo.util.mineral

Class ReservoirMercuryEstimator

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.util.mineral.ReservoirMercuryEstimator
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class ReservoirMercuryEstimator extends Object implements Serializable
Estimates the upper limits of elemental mercury in a reservoir fluid from mineral equilibrium.

Two condensed phases can hold mercury back in a reservoir. Mercury sulfide (cinnabar or metacinnabar, or mercury held as a dilute sulfide component in pyrite) limits the mercury fugacity through 4 HgS + CH4 + 2 H2O = 4 Hg + 4 H2S + CO2, so that 4 ln f(Hg) = ln K(T,P) + ln f(CH4) + 2 ln a(H2O) + 4 ln a(HgS) - 4 ln f(H2S) - ln f(CO2). Liquid mercury limits it at the vapour pressure with the pressure correction. The fugacities of CH4, CO2 and H2S come from the equation of state of the fluid. Mercury is treated as a dilute solute: its fugacity coefficient in each fluid phase is taken at trace content, and the mercury content of the whole fluid at a limit is the limiting fugacity divided by the fugacity coefficient and pressure, summed over the phases. The error is of the order of the mercury mole fraction.

The H2S fugacity is either that of the fluid (measured H2S) or that of the pyrite and Fe-carbonate buffer used by ReservoirH2SEstimator, in which case the reaction becomes 8 HgS + 4 FeCO3 + CH4 = 8 Hg + 4 FeS2 + 5 CO2 + 2 H2O and no H2S measurement is needed.

The results are limits, not predictions. The sulfide limit rises by about a factor of 20 per 30 °C, so that in cool reservoirs (below about 80-100 °C) the sulfide can hold mercury to low levels, while in hot reservoirs the limit lies far above what source rocks supply and the mercury content is set by supply. A measured content is compared with the limit through the saturation index of ReservoirMercuryEstimator.Estimate.getSulfideSaturationIndex(). A mercury sulfide activity below one represents mercury held as a trace component of pyrite or other sulfides.

      Estimates the mercury limits of a reservoir fluid at its temperature and pressure.
      Parameters:
      fluid - reservoir fluid containing methane and CO2, and H2S when the H2S basis is the fluid. Mercury is added as a trace if absent; if present, its content is compared with the limits. The fluid is not modified.

    • sulfideSaturationTemperature

      public double sulfideSaturationTemperature(SystemInterface fluid, double mercuryMoleFraction, double lowTemperature, double highTemperature)
      Finds the temperature at which a mercury content equals the sulfide limit of the fluid.

      The sulfide limit rises monotonically with temperature at fixed composition and pressure. Above the returned temperature the sulfide cannot hold the given mercury content back; below it the fluid is supersaturated and mercury sulfide can form. The search uses bisection in temperature with the full equation-of-state solution.

      Parameters:
      fluid - reservoir fluid at its pressure (its temperature is not used); not modified
      mercuryMoleFraction - mercury content of the reservoir fluid [mole fraction]
      lowTemperature - lower bound of the search [K]
      highTemperature - upper bound of the search [K]
      Returns:
      temperature [K], or Double.NaN if the content lies outside the limits between the bounds
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the content is not positive or the bounds are not increasing
